extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and marketers who write and distribute event press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and distributing press releases specifically to announce and promote events; covers structure, content, pitching, journalist expectations, and using AI/templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send your event press release to the right journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch to relevant journalists and bloggers—people who are interested in writing about your event; avoid the 'spray and pray' method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify relevant contacts using a media contacts database (e.g., search by keywords to find journalists who wrote about similar events). Further refine by filtering location and topics/industries. Only send info that is useful to the outlet/journalist; do not flood unrelated outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of event press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize which of the common types your release is: (1) upcoming closed events where you invite journalists or announce they will take place, (2) closed events that have already taken place, (3) upcoming open events intended to invite media audiences, (4) open events that have already taken place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the type to frame content, who to send it to, and the call to action (e.g., RSVP vs. recap).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the proper release format
rubrics_metrics.description: An event press release follows the same format as any other press release; include specific elements in each section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure to include: Headline, Lead, Body, Date of publishing (timeliness), Boilerplate, and Contact information. Whether using a template or writing from scratch, ensure each element is present and serves its function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline — concise and newsworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should be concise, attention-grabbing, and reflect the event's main theme or news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients scan the headline in a fraction of a second—focus on the main takeaway and convince media that the event is newsworthy within limited characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead/subheader — answer the basics and engage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the lead to expand on what makes the event worth media attention; the first paragraph should provide a concise and engaging summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer who, what, when, where, and why in the first paragraph and use the lead as a de facto extension of the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide event details (body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elaborate on the event's purpose, significance, notable features or guest speakers, date, time, location, and background/history in subsequent paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a press release, not advertisement—avoid salesy language. Focus on information that helps a journalist write a useful article, not promotional copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Add quotes from key organizers, sponsors, or speakers to add credibility and a human element to the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensible, fact-anchored quotes that provide perspective or insight rather than empty praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include extra information (guests, sponsors, partners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share details about special guests, performers, noteworthy activities, and mention any sponsors or partners involved in the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics that make the story compelling and explain relevance to the audience; include known comparators for niche items so general audiences understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add your boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a short paragraph about your organization at the end of the press release (the boilerplate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate concise and informative—background that helps journalists contextualize the organizer/company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include media contact person's name, phone number, and email address and ensure this person is readily available to answer media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make contact details clear and double-check availability; media need a direct, responsive contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate newsworthiness (focus on main takeaway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convince media contacts that your event is newsworthy by focusing headline/lead on the event's main takeaway or news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the element of the event that will matter to the outlet's audience and make that the central message rather than promotional fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'fluffy' or promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overuse adjectives, praises, exaggerations, 'cool words', or excessive capitalization; avoid phrases like 'We are happy to announce' that add no factual value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists prefer figures, facts, and sensible quotes. Keep language factual and work to the outlet's standards rather than marketing copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present solid facts that interest the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide substantive facts (data, trends, forecasts, specific topics of talks) rather than vague positive statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, include specifics like investment figures, trend data, or clear descriptions of topics and speakers; for niche events, give known comparisons so readers understand context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add images and supporting attachments correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Include good pictures and attachments of appropriate size and format to support coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t rely solely on links to social pages. Attachments should be easy to download and use; photos are especially important for grand openings and visually-driven events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up correctly with journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate follow-up practices: email follow-ups are preferred; calling is typically frowned upon unless you know the journalist or can offer missing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid calling like telemarketing or repeatedly sending the same release to multiple addresses at an outlet (this can land you in spam). If you call, prepare a clear, respectful approach and only do so when it adds value (e.g., clarifying missing info).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send irrelevant releases to outlets (check fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sending, ask: Does the outlet cover similar events? Does the journalist cover the subject? Will the journalist find all necessary info? Is the main point enough for the outlet to publish?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inviting a journalist, also send an actual invitation (with date/time/venue) besides the press release when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates and tools to ensure completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press release templates (or Prowly's templates/creator) to include all important elements that journalists expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates speed up the process and help ensure format and required content are present; customize rather than blindly paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an event press release with AI — required inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: When using AI tools, enter basic details (type of release, target audience, language) and be specific in key messages (Purpose, Event Highlights, Call to Action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise key messages: purpose (goal/significance), event highlights (speakers/activities), and clear instructions for RSVP/media credentials. Expect follow-up questions from the tool to flesh out the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an event press release with AI — review and customization
rubrics_metrics.description: After generating a draft with AI, customize and edit the draft (style, length, header fonts) and apply editorial judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An AI assistant can suggest improvements (the article notes a review based on '11 key criteria') but you must fine-tune tone, remove promotional language, and verify facts and contact details before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to get contact recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools can suggest journalists to pitch based on keywords found in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the suggestions as a starting point but always research contacts individually to confirm beat/fit and to find recent relevant work.
